notes.meaning: God revealed Himself to His chosen people by rescuing them in times of trouble. His name became famous and respected across the land because He proved His power to save. Those who know God can celebrate His greatness and put their confidence in Him.

Salem was an ancient name for Jerusalem, and Mount Zion was the hill where God set up His temple. God chose this place as His earthly home among His people. Because He lived in their midst, the city enjoyed His special favor and protection.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: Augustine read God's dwelling "in peace" as a picture of the heart. You make room for God inside you by confessing your sins.

notes.meaning: Right at Jerusalem, God destroyed the weapons of the attacking enemy army. Flaming arrows, shields, and swords were broken so they could do no harm. God ended the entire conflict with one stroke of His power.

God shines with brilliant light and majesty. He is far greater than the mighty kingdoms of the world, which act like mountains full of wild beasts hunting for prey. While earthly empires build their power through violence, God's royal glory outshines them all.

Proud and boastful soldiers came expecting to rob the city, but they ended up losing everything. God struck them down so that they slept the sleep of death. The strongest warriors suddenly lost all their strength and could not even lift their hands to fight.

A single rebuke from the God of Jacob was enough to freeze the whole enemy force. Both the war horses and the men riding in chariots fell completely silent in death. The victory was won by God's powerful voice, not by human weapons.

God alone deserves deep awe and holy fear. When His righteous anger begins to burn against sin, no army or human being can stand against Him. His great power reminds everyone to treat Him with reverence and respect.

God announced His final verdict from heaven, and the whole earth grew silent with fear. When His judgment fell upon the invaders, other nations were terrified to cause any more trouble. A quiet hush spread over the land before His mighty authority.

God stood up like a fair judge to take action. His purpose in punishing the proud enemy was to rescue the humble, helpless people who trusted Him. His judgments bring ruin to bullies but safety to those who walk quietly with Him.

Even the furious rage of wicked men ends up bringing praise to God. When enemies attack, God overrules their fury to show His own power, wisdom, and justice. He also sets a strict boundary on their rage, stopping whatever does not serve His holy plan.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars think the Hebrew text is unclear here and suggest a small correction. Then the verse would mean that those who escaped the enemy's anger hold a feast of thanks to God.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: The old Greek and Latin Bibles read the verse differently. They say that human thought will praise God, and what remains of it will keep a feast day for him.

notes.meaning: God's people are told to make solemn promises of thanksgiving and make sure to pay them. When God delivers us, we should show our thankfulness with real devotion and praise. Neighboring nations are also invited to bring tribute and honor to the awesome God.

other.label: Catholic and Orthodox
other.view: Augustine taught that the psalm says "vow and pay," not "don't vow." Every believer should vow to believe, to hope for eternal life, and to live a godly life, and God's help makes it possible.

notes.meaning: God easily snips away the breath and courage of proud rulers, just like a worker cuts a bunch of grapes from a vine. Earthly kings must give an account to Him, and they tremble before His majesty. No human leader is too powerful for God to humble.
